unstated.behaviour: No FEN validation. Missing/undefined/null/42 -> TypeError from internals ('Cannot read properties of undefined (reading \'trim\')', 'fen.trim is not a function'), except applyMove() with no arguments, which throws IllegalMoveError 'Expected a legal UCI move string'. '' / 'not-a-fen' / 7 ranks -> TypeError 'ranks[rank] is not iterable'. Side-to-move 'x' or 'W' -> legalMoves [] and status 'stalemate'. 9-square rank, 7-square rank, unknown letter 'x', castling 'XYZ', en-passant 'z9', 9 ranks all accepted; applyMove echoes the damage ('.../97/...', 'ppppxppp', 'ppppppp1', 'b XYZ'). Missing clocks or '1.5' -> BigInt TypeError/SyntaxError. Leading/trailing whitespace and newline tolerated. Impossible positions (no kings -> 'stalemate'; two kings; pawn on 8th; side not to move in check) return values.
unstated.evidence: node .audit/unstated.js (U-1 block) printed each result as listed.

unstated.behaviour: Only exact lowercase UCI that matches a legal move is accepted (regex /^[a-h][1-8][a-h][1-8][qrbn]?$/ then a legal-move match). 'E2E4', ' e2e4', 'e2e4 ', 'e4', 'e2-e4', 'e2xe4', 'e2e4q', 'e2e9', 42, null, undefined, ['e2e4'], 'e1h1', 'e1a1', bare 'e7e8', 'e7e8Q' all throw IllegalMoveError. With e8 free ('3k4/4P3/... w'), e7e8q/r/b/n put Q/R/B/N on e8. On the inventory fen '4k3/4P3/...' the black king blocks e8, so every e7e8 variant is rightly rejected.

class IllegalMoveError extends Error; instanceof IllegalMoveError and Error both true; constructor.name and name 'IllegalMoveError'; message 'Illegal move: e2e5' / 'Illegal move: a1a3' (names the move, not the FEN); for a non-string 'Expected a legal UCI move string'; stack present; own keys ['name']; no move/fen properties.

Rights are not trusted: 'w K' with no rook, 'w KQ' with no h1 rook (only e1c1 offered, which is legal), king on e2 with 'K' -> no e1g1; e1g1 throws IllegalMoveError. A rights letter whose rook square holds an enemy rook is not honoured. A stale right stays in the FEN after other moves (a1a2 from 'R3K3 w KQ' -> 'K'). En-passant square e3 with white to move, and ep squares with no pawn behind them, are ignored (no capture onto them).
All published perft counts match: start d3 8902, d4 197281; Kiwipete d1 48, d2 2039, d3 97862; position 3 d4 43238; also position 4 d3 9467, position 5 d3 62379, position 6 d3 89890.

spec_notes: spec.md is short and consistent with the request; it cites request clauses (S1-S11) by its own numbering. R-1 decides 'The input contract is valid orthodox FEN' in an ordinary requirement line, without saying what happens otherwise (the product does no validation, so malformed FENs give confident wrong answers). R-3 decides strict legal-UCI input with IllegalMoveError for anything else, unmarked. R-4 decides no draw statuses (consistent with the request's four values). It does not state that IllegalMoveError is exported, that castling may not start in or pass through check, or the king-two-square UCI castling form (architecture.md AD-1 and the README cover these). It pins test ids TC-1..TC-8 to requirements, which a correct build need not share.
tests_notes: All tests use only the public API and full FEN or move-list comparisons; none touch internals or file names. Several tests bundle behaviours: TC-2 both mates; TC-5 promotions plus unrelated illegal-UCI checks on the start position; the second TC-3 test mixes out-of/through/into check, blocked path and missing rights/rook; TC-6 stalemate, check replies and a pin; TC-8 both timing limits (wall clock, generous margins). Every IllegalMoveError check is assert.throws(fn, IllegalMoveError), which degrades to 'throws anything' if the export disappears: removing the export left 10/10 passing. No test passes an invalid FEN, and no test asserts the error's name or message. Nothing found that would fail on another correct build.
maintainer: Everything is one 336-line file on a 0x88 board, with boardAfter shared by legality filtering, castling transit checks and move application, so a change there affects generation and application at once. parseFen does no validation, so adding it changes what all three entry points throw for bad input and needs new tests, because the suite has none for invalid FENs and its error-class checks would not notice a missing export.
